scope: Secret/credential touchpoint detection. Synthetic touchpoints.py emits 8 records, deterministically, in every stdin environment: 3 env reads (env_read) + 2 two-arg defaults (env_default — os.getenv(KEY, default) and os.environ.get(KEY, default), the two idiomatic spellings of the #1470 Fail-Fast violation) + 1 dotenv load, plus 1 password_literal + 1 aws_access_key from the ripgrep stage. The ripgrep records ARE counted in the floor, because the stage is now stdin-independent: it is invoked with an explicit `.` path target. Previously it passed no target, so rg recursed the CWD only when stdin was a character device or closed, and CONSUMED stdin when stdin was a pipe or a regular file — the pre-commit / pre-push / CI path. That made password_literal, aws_access_key and aws_secret_key emit ZERO records in every automated context while still firing by hand from a terminal: a fail-OPEN secret gate. Measured before the fix: a file carrying AKIA-prefixed keys and a password literal passed the sst3-sec hook clean, and emitted 2 records under `< /dev/null`. Fixed under Issue #530 Stage 5 with an AP #18 sample invocation across 3 repo shapes. The floor of 8 is discriminating in both directions: dropping EITHER env_default pattern yields 7 and dropping both yields 6, so a wrapper that loses either spelling fails this fixture. stdout_kind_records env_default is retained as a belt-and-braces assertion that survives any future renumbering of the floor.
